housing.summary: Rotterdam's rental market is competitive but generally more affordable than Amsterdam. Most listings are found via online portals and agents (makelaars); furnished and unfurnished options both common. Expats often use rental agencies, and many landlords require proof of income (typically 3-4x monthly rent) and Dutch bank account details.

banking.summary: Opening a Dutch bank account typically requires a BSN (citizen service number), proof of address (registration), passport/ID, and sometimes proof of employment. Major banks offer expat-friendly onboarding; some digital banks allow account opening before BSN issuance.

schools.summary: Rotterdam offers Dutch public schools, bilingual programs, and several international schools serving the expat community. International options follow British, IB, and other curricula. Public education is free or low-cost; international schools charge tuition.

legal_admin.summary: New residents staying longer than four months must register with the municipality (Gemeente Rotterdam) to receive a BSN. EU/EEA citizens register directly; non-EU nationals typically need a residence permit (IND) first. Registration requires a rental contract or proof of address and a valid ID.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register in the Basisregistratie Personen (BRP) at Gemeente Rotterdam to obtain a BSN

tax_finance.summary: Income tax is administered nationally by the Belastingdienst (Dutch Tax Administration). Residents are taxed on worldwide income; qualifying skilled migrants may benefit from the 30% ruling. The BSN doubles as the tax identification number.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: BSN (Burgerservicenummer, also serves as tax ID)

transport.summary: Rotterdam has an extensive public transport network run by RET, covering metro, tram, and bus lines, integrated with regional rail. Travel uses the OV-chipkaart (or contactless/OVpay). The city is highly bike-friendly with dedicated cycling infrastructure.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid; non-EU licences generally must be exchanged for a Dutch licence within a set period after registration, sometimes requiring a Dutch driving test unless a bilateral exchange or 30% ruling exemption applies.
transport.healthcare_registration: Residents must take out mandatory Dutch basic health insurance (basisverzekering) within four months of registration and register with a local GP (huisarts).
